courses.name: Fundamentals of Programming and Computational Problem Solving
courses.description: Introduces object-oriented programming in Python and a statically typed language, using AI and ML in programming exercises.

courses.name: Software Design & Composition
courses.description: Develops software design, specification, testing and debugging skills, including recursion and inductive data structures.

courses.name: Data Structures & Algorithms (Formerly Comp_Sci 214)
courses.description: Analyzes and implements data structures and algorithms for collections, graphs, searching, sorting and shortest paths.
courses.prerequisites: One of COMP_SCI150 /GEN_ENG150 /GEN_ENG151, plus COMP_SCI180. Concurrent COMP_SCI211 enrollment is prohibited.

courses.name: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Introduces AI knowledge representation and problem solving, including theorem proving, vision and neural networks.

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.description: Studies learning algorithms including Bayesian methods, decision trees, neural networks, Markov models and reinforcement learning.

Eligibility
requirements.summary: Open to undergraduate students except CS BS, WCAS CS major, and AI major students. CS students may use their major AI concentration instead.

requirements.title: Planning and declaration
requirements.summary: Begin before the end of the first junior-year quarter; declare through MAS by the end of junior year.

requirements.title: Distinct coursework
requirements.summary: At least four units must be unique to this minor, unused by other minors, certificates, or any major requirements. They may also satisfy McCormick humanities/social sciences, WCAS distribution, or unrestricted electives.

notes: Parsed program-specific requirements and policies. Topic variants have distinct IDs; alternative listings do not create additional course slots. Catalog labels units; no conversion to semester hours.

Course source IDs retain the minor/thread eligibility provenance. No credits inferred by dividing program totals; variable-credit topics remain unknown when not explicitly fixed.
